hints: Remember that an ester is made from a carboxylic acid plus an alcohol, so try splitting the ester back into those two parts.
Look at the right-hand side, $\text{OCH}_3$. That single carbon fragment must have come from a 1-carbon alcohol.
Now look at the left-hand side, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}$. Count the carbons to work out which acid supplies that acyl group.
walkthrough:
**Recall how esters form**

Esters are made by esterification of a carboxylic acid with an alcohol in the presence of concentrated sulfuric acid.

General equation:
$$\text{RCOOH} + \text{R'OH} \rightleftharpoons \text{RCOOR'} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Split the given ester into two parts**

Think of the ester as acid part + alcohol part. The $\text{CO}_2$ in the middle is really the $\text{COO}$ link.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_3 = \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO} | \text{OCH}_3$$

**Identify the alcohol and the acid**

The $\text{OCH}_3$ part comes from the alcohol, so the alcohol is $\text{CH}_3\text{OH}$, methanol. The $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}$ part comes from the acid, so the acid is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$, propanoic acid.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH} + \text{CH}_3\text{OH} \rightleftharpoons \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOCH}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

options.A: Ethanol ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$) plus ethanoic acid ($\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$) would give ethyl ethanoate, $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. This has the 2-carbon fragment on the wrong side of the ester link.
options.B: Methanol ($\text{CH}_3\text{OH}$) plus ethanoic acid ($\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$) would give methyl ethanoate, $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_3$. This is one carbon too short on the acid side, it lacks the extra $\text{CH}_2$.
options.C: Methanol supplies the $\text{OCH}_3$ part and propanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$, supplies the $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}$ part. Together they correctly form methyl propanoate, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_3$ plus water.
options.D: Propan-1-ol ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$) plus methanoic acid ($\text{HCOOH}$) would give propyl methanoate, $\text{HCO}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. This reverses the sizes of the two sides, giving a 1-carbon acid part and a 3-carbon alcohol part.
